supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic gems and gospel vibes shine in brief set
ai_show_review.blurb: The 30‑minute acoustic set delivers strong renditions of "To Lay Me Down", "Rosa Lee McFall" and a soulful "Swing Low (Sweet Chariot)". Jerry’s vocals lead the way while Phil provides rich bass support; the mix is generally clear though low‑end can be muddy. A good snapshot of the Dead’s folk‑rock/gospel side, recommended for its intimate feel.
ai_show_review.review:
On July 30, 1970 at Lion’s Share the Grateful Dead offered a short, 30‑minute acoustic set that feels like a warm family gathering rather than a full‑blown concert. The band walks through folk‑rock and gospel territory with confidence – “To Lay Me Down” opens the night with gentle strumming, followed by the playful romp of “Me And My Uncle”, the howl of “Dire Wolf”, and the sweet storytelling of “Candyman”. Highlights include the heartfelt “Rosa Lee McFall”, the soaring a cappella moment on “A Voice From On High*”, and Jerry Garcia’s resonant vocal on the traditional “Swing Low (Sweet Chariot)”.  

Two soundboard recordings capture this set. The Cotsman‑sourced tape (gd70-07-30.sbd.cotsman.17077.sbeok.shnf) is praised for its overall clarity and balanced presentation, only marred by a occasionally muddy low‑end that can submerge some of Jerry’s guitar nuance. The Boswell transfer (gd1970-07-30.sbd.boswell.smith.114020.flac16) suffers from noticeable hiss due to multiple generations of copying but still conveys the same intimate vibe, especially when the New Riders of the Purple Sage guests add extra texture. For listeners seeking the cleanest and most complete listening experience, the Cotsman recording is the recommended choice.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: One recording is clearly positive, praising the acoustic set and standout songs; the second is mixed due to tape hiss but does not criticize the performance itself. Overall sentiment about the music is modestly positive with no consistent negative remarks, justifying a moderate +0.8 adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Clear soundboard capture with good overall balance; highlights the acoustic set while keeping tape hiss low and preserving vocal clarity.

key_highlights: Lovely acoustic set featuring folk‑rock and gospel numbers.
Jerry Garcia’s vocals shine on "Swing Low (Sweet Chariot)" and "A Voice From On High*".
Phil Lesh delivers rich, supportive bass lines despite occasional mix mud.
Good soundboard quality overall; low‑end muddiness is the only notable flaw.

band_performance.Jerry: Strong vocal presence on "Swing Low" and other numbers; guitar sometimes buried by forward bass in the mix.
band_performance.Phil: Rich, supportive bass lines that drive the acoustic set, though occasional mix dominance muddies clarity.
